newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee nuke plant extends shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee nuke plant extends shutdown.

text.p: The shutdown of the Maine Yankee nuclear plant has been extended after an additional problem was discovered in an electrical cable system, officials said Monday.

The 910-megawatt facility, which was taken off-line Dec. 6, will remain shut down "for several more weeks" so additional cable systems can be inspected, spokesperson Maureen Brown said in a statement.

The 24-year-old plant was taken off-line when workers discovered that two electrical cables in the reactor control system had been installed improperly and did not conform with engineering safety requirements.
Maine Yankee decided to expand the review to other cable systems after workers Friday discovered an instalation problem of with electrical cables n the Primary Auxiliary Building, according to Brown.

In both cases the cables were not properly seperated from each other, which would potentially undermines the control system's required redundancy, according to officials familiar with the plant's design.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
